uncited: *   **Input:** Low-resolution similarity map $S_L$ (dimensions $N_L \times N_L \times N_L$ or similar), Raw intensity volume $V$ (dimensions $N_V \times N_V \times N_V$).
**Bilateral Grid:** A 3D grid where each cell stores aggregated color (intensity) and position information.
The grid resolution is determined by the parameters $\sigma$ (spatial) and $\sigma_r$ (range/intensity).
**Similarity Map:** A 3D volume of float values representing the confidence or similarity of a voxel belonging to a structure.
**Tri-linear Upsampling:** Upsample the low-resolution similarity map $S_L$ tri-linearly to match the resolution of the raw volume $V$ (or the target resolution $N_H$).
**Cropping:** Crop the regions where the similarity value $S_{up} > \tau$ to discard low-similarity areas.
**3D Bilateral Solver Execution:** Solve for the smoothed high-resolution similarity $S_H$ using the cropped region from $V$ as the reference image for edge-awareness.
*   **Block Artifacts:** Caused by the $\sigma$ parameters of the bilateral solver, which control the window used for blurring.
*   **Time Complexity:** The post-processing time varies with resolution.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
The 3D Fast Bilateral Solver is a 3D extension to the Fast Bilateral Solver (BLS) [12], originally proposed for 2D images.
